newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar strengthens on commission buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar strengthens on commission buying.

text.p: Commission house buying drove London's October white sugar contract higher in the early part of Monday's session with a mixed bag of sellers also taking advantage of the gains, traders said.
The firm start to the week was seen as a continuation of the fund-led buying spree late on Friday which kept the front contract above the $321.70 resistance point broken earlier in the week.
One leading commission house led on the buy side, thought to be for a trade customer, while sellers were noted among various brokers and other commission houses.
At 1110 GMT October was up $2.00 at an intraday high of $325.30 and December up $1.70 at $320.90. Volume was concentrated in October and totalled 427 lots.
Technical analysts pegged resistance at $330 after October breached $321.70, now considered the initial support point. Other downside barriers were placed at $318.50 and $314.50.
The spot contract is following an upward trendline dating from the $306.50 peak scored at the end of October 1996.
Traders said fresh fundamental news was thin, noting that results were still awaited in Bangladesh's recent tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of white crystal sugar for shipment by September 9.
The Paris market followed a similar pattern to London although volume was thin at just 72 lots.
October was up $2.50 at $324.50 and December up $2.00 at $320.00. Nothing was traded on the lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA white sugar market.
